  "content": "import { Router } from \"express\";\nimport { eq, sql, type SQL } from \"drizzle-orm\";\nimport type { Article, ApiError, Paginated } from \"@carma/shared\";\nimport { db } from \"../db/index.js\";\nimport { articles, sources } from \"../db/schema.js\";\nimport { CursorError, decodeCursor, encodeCursor } from \"../lib/cursor.js\";\n\nexport const articlesRouter = Router();\n\nconst DEFAULT_LIMIT = 5;\nconst MAX_LIMIT = 50;\n\n// Ordering that matches the articles_published_at_id_idx index. NULLS LAST is\n// required so the planner uses the index instead of sorting (see README).\nconst ORDER_DESC = sql`${articles.publishedAt} DESC NULLS LAST, ${articles.id} DESC NULLS LAST`;\n// Reverse of the index — used when paging backward; results are reversed back\n// to DESC for presentation.\nconst ORDER_ASC = sql`${articles.publishedAt} ASC NULLS FIRST, ${articles.id} ASC NULLS FIRST`;\n\nfunction parseLimit(raw: unknown): number {\n  const n = Number(raw);\n  if (Number.isInteger(n) && n > 0) return Math.min(n, MAX_LIMIT);\n  return DEFAULT_LIMIT;\n}\n\n/** Is there a row strictly older than this keyset position? (forward exists) */\nasync function hasOlder(publishedAt: Date, id: number): Promise<boolean> {\n  const rows = await db\n    .select({ one: sql`1` })\n    .from(articles)\n    .where(sql`(${articles.publishedAt}, ${articles.id}) < (${publishedAt}, ${id})`)\n    .limit(1);\n  return rows.length > 0;\n}\n\n/** Is there a row strictly newer than this keyset position? (backward exists) */\nasync function hasNewer(publishedAt: Date, id: number): Promise<boolean> {\n  const rows = await db\n    .select({ one: sql`1` })\n    .from(articles)\n    .where(sql`(${articles.publishedAt}, ${articles.id}) > (${publishedAt}, ${id})`)\n    .limit(1);\n  return rows.length > 0;\n}\n\n// GET /api/articles?limit=5&cursor=<token>&direction=next|prev\n// Keyset-paginated, newest-first. Without a cursor, returns the first page.\narticlesRouter.get(\"/\", async (req, res) => {\n  const limit = parseLimit(req.query.limit);\n  const direction = req.query.direction === \"prev\" ? \"prev\" : \"next\";\n  const cursorToken =\n    typeof req.query.cursor === \"string\" && req.query.cursor.length > 0\n      ? req.query.cursor\n      : undefined;\n\n  let where: SQL | undefined;\n  let orderBy: SQL = ORDER_DESC;\n  let reversed = false;\n\n  if (cursorToken) {\n    let cursor;\n    try {\n      cursor = decodeCursor(cursorToken);\n    } catch (err) {\n      if (err instanceof CursorError) {\n        const body: ApiError = { error: err.message };\n        return res.status(400).json(body);\n      }\n      throw err;\n    }\n\n    if (direction === \"prev\") {\n      // Rows newer than the page's first edge, scanned ascending (closest-first)\n      // then reversed back to newest-first.\n      where = sql`(${articles.publishedAt}, ${articles.id}) > (${new Date(cursor.f.t)}, ${cursor.f.i})`;\n      orderBy = ORDER_ASC;\n      reversed = true;\n    } else {\n      // Rows older than the page's last edge.\n      where = sql`(${articles.publishedAt}, ${articles.id}) < (${new Date(cursor.l.t)}, ${cursor.l.i})`;\n    }\n  }\n\n  const query = db\n    .select({\n      id: articles.id,\n      headline: articles.headline,\n      body: articles.body,\n      source: sources.name,\n      publishedAt: articles.publishedAt,\n      createdAt: articles.createdAt,\n    })\n    .from(articles)\n    .innerJoin(sources, eq(articles.sourceId, sources.id))\n    .$dynamic();\n\n  if (where) query.where(where);\n  const rows = await query.orderBy(orderBy).limit(limit);\n  if (reversed) rows.reverse();\n\n  if (rows.length === 0) {\n    const body: Paginated<Article> = {\n      data: [],\n      pageInfo: { cursor: null, hasNext: false, hasPrev: false },\n    };\n    return res.json(body);\n  }\n\n  const first = rows[0]!;\n  const last = rows[rows.length - 1]!;\n\n  // Probe both edges so hasNext/hasPrev are correct regardless of which\n  // direction we navigated (index-only LIMIT 1 lookups).\n  const [hasPrev, hasNext] = await Promise.all([\n    hasNewer(first.publishedAt, first.id),\n    hasOlder(last.publishedAt, last.id),\n  ]);\n\n  const cursor = encodeCursor({\n    f: { t: first.publishedAt.toISOString(), i: first.id },\n    l: { t: last.publishedAt.toISOString(), i: last.id },\n  });\n\n  const data: Article[] = rows.map((row) => ({\n    id: row.id,\n    headline: row.headline,\n    body: row.body,\n    source: row.source,\n    publishedAt: row.publishedAt.toISOString(),\n    createdAt: row.createdAt.toISOString(),\n  }));\n\n  const body: Paginated<Article> = {\n    data,\n    pageInfo: { cursor, hasNext, hasPrev },\n  };\n  res.json(body);\n});\n"
}

## 🤖 Assistant  
<sub>2026-07-25T15:16:19.420Z</sub>

Bidirectional keyset pagination is implemented and verified end-to-end.

## How it works
- **`GET /api/articles?limit=5&cursor=<token>&direction=next|prev`** — no cursor = first page (newest); default **5/page** (capped at 50).
- **The cursor token encodes *both* page edges** — the first row and last row as `(publishedAt, id)` pairs — so a single token navigates either way:
  - `direction=next` → `WHERE (published_at, id) < lastEdge` (older), DESC.
  - `direction=prev` → `WHERE (published_at, id) > firstEdge` (newer), scanned ASC then reversed for display.
- **Response** is `Paginated<Article>` = `{ data, pageInfo: { cursor, hasNext, hasPrev } }`. `hasNext`/`hasPrev` come from two tiny index-only `LIMIT 1` boundary probes, so they're correct no matter which direction you came from.

## New/changed files
- `packages/shared/src/index.ts` — `PageInfo` + `Paginated<T>`.
- `apps/api/src/lib/cursor.ts` — base64url encode/decode of the both-edges cursor, with validation (`CursorError` → 400).
- `apps/api/src/routes/articles.ts` — the keyset query (forward/back), edge probes, `NULLS LAST` ordering matching the index.

## Verified
- Default **5/page**; forward `1–5 → 6–10 → 11–15`; **backward round-trips exactly** (`p3 →prev→ p2`, `→prev→ p1` restore the original pages, and `hasPrev` flips back to `false` on page 1).
- Walked all **4 pages / 20 rows**; last page `[16–20]` with `hasNext=false, hasPrev=true`.
- No overlap across pages, strict descending order, `limit=3` honored, malformed cursor → **400** with a clear message.
- `EXPLAIN`: the keyset predicate uses **`Index Scan using articles_published_at_id_idx`** (no Sort node), with the source join as a `sources_pkey` lookup — exactly the plan the indexes were designed for.

## One thing to note
The frontend (`useArticles`) reads `body.data`, so it still works — but it now shows only the **first 5** articles with no Prev/Next controls yet (this pass was the backend system, as asked). 

Two small follow-ups worth flagging:
- **Frontend UI** — wire Prev/Next buttons to `pageInfo` (I can do this next if you want it demonstrable in the browser).
- **Cursor timestamp precision** — the token uses millisecond ISO (JS `Date`), which is exact for your second-granularity data; if you ever store sub-millisecond `published_at`, the cursor would need microsecond encoding. I left a note in the code's intent but can make it microsecond-safe now if you'd prefer.

Want me to hook up the frontend Prev/Next controls?

{
  "file_path": "/Users/garythrels/Development/personal/carma/apps/web/src/hooks/useArticles.ts",
  "content": "import { Paginated, Article } from \"@carma/shared\";\nimport { useCallback, useEffect, useState } from \"react\";\nimport { ArticlesState } from \"../types\";\n\n/** What page to request: the current page's cursor + which way to move from it. */\ninterface PageRequest {\n  cursor: string | null;\n  direction: \"next\" | \"prev\";\n}\n\n/**\n * Keyset-paginated articles. The API returns a single `cursor` token per page\n * that encodes both edges, so we navigate by re-requesting with that same cursor\n * plus a direction. `goNext`/`goPrev` are no-ops when there's no further page.\n */\nexport function useArticles(limit = 5) {\n  const [request, setRequest] = useState<PageRequest>({\n    cursor: null,\n    direction: \"next\",\n  });\n  const [state, setState] = useState<ArticlesState>({ status: \"loading\" });\n  const [isFetching, setIsFetching] = useState(true);\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    const controller = new AbortController();\n    setIsFetching(true);\n\n    async function load() {\n      const params = new URLSearchParams({ limit: String(limit) });\n      if (request.cursor) {\n        params.set(\"cursor\", request.cursor);\n        params.set(\"direction\", request.direction);\n      }\n\n      try {\n        const res = await fetch(`/api/articles?${params.toString()}`, {\n          signal: controller.signal,\n        });\n        if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`Request failed: ${res.status}`);\n        const body = (await res.json()) as Paginated<Article>;\n        setState({\n          status: \"ready\",\n          articles: body.data,\n          pageInfo: body.pageInfo,\n        });\n      } catch (err) {\n        if (controller.signal.aborted) return;\n        setState({\n          status: \"error\",\n          message: err instanceof Error ? err.message : \"Unknown error\",\n        });\n      } finally {\n        if (!controller.signal.aborted) setIsFetching(false);\n      }\n    }\n\n    void load();\n    return () => controller.abort();\n  }, [request, limit]);\n\n  const goNext = useCallback(() => {\n    setState((s) => {\n      if (s.status === \"ready\" && s.pageInfo.hasNext && s.pageInfo.cursor) {\n        setRequest({ cursor: s.pageInfo.cursor, direction: \"next\" });\n      }\n      return s;\n    });\n  }, []);\n\n  const goPrev = useCallback(() => {\n    setState((s) => {\n      if (s.status === \"ready\" && s.pageInfo.hasPrev && s.pageInfo.cursor) {\n        setRequest({ cursor: s.pageInfo.cursor, direction: \"prev\" });\n      }\n      return s;\n    });\n  }, []);\n\n  return { state, isFetching, goNext, goPrev };\n}\n"
}

  "content": "import { PageInfo } from \"@carma/shared\";\nimport { useCallback, useRef, useState } from \"react\";\n\n/** What page to request: the current page's cursor + which way to move from it. */\nexport interface CursorRequest {\n  cursor: string | null;\n  direction: \"next\" | \"prev\";\n}\n\n/**\n * Reusable keyset-pagination navigation. Owns the `request` (cursor + direction)\n * that a data hook feeds into its fetch, and derives `goNext`/`goPrev` from the\n * latest `PageInfo`. Not tied to any particular resource — pass it the `PageInfo`\n * of whatever cursor-paginated endpoint you're consuming.\n *\n *   const { request, goNext, goPrev } = useCursorPagination(pageInfo);\n *   // fetch using `request`, then render buttons wired to goNext/goPrev.\n */\nexport function useCursorPagination(pageInfo: PageInfo | null) {\n  const [request, setRequest] = useState<CursorRequest>({\n    cursor: null,\n    direction: \"next\",\n  });\n\n  // Keep the latest pageInfo in a ref so goNext/goPrev stay referentially stable\n  // while always reading current values.\n  const pageInfoRef = useRef<PageInfo | null>(pageInfo);\n  pageInfoRef.current = pageInfo;\n\n  const goNext = useCallback(() => {\n    const pi = pageInfoRef.current;\n    if (pi?.hasNext && pi.cursor) {\n      setRequest({ cursor: pi.cursor, direction: \"next\" });\n    }\n  }, []);\n\n  const goPrev = useCallback(() => {\n    const pi = pageInfoRef.current;\n    if (pi?.hasPrev && pi.cursor) {\n      setRequest({ cursor: pi.cursor, direction: \"prev\" });\n    }\n  }, []);\n\n  return {\n    request,\n    goNext,\n    goPrev,\n    canNext: pageInfo?.hasNext ?? false,\n    canPrev: pageInfo?.hasPrev ?? false,\n  };\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/garythrels/Development/personal/carma/apps/web/src/hooks/useArticles.ts",
  "content": "import { Paginated, Article } from \"@carma/shared\";\nimport { useEffect, useRef, useState } from \"react\";\nimport { ArticlesState } from \"../types\";\nimport { useCursorPagination } from \"./useCursorPagination\";\n\n/**\n * Keyset-paginated articles. Navigation (cursor + direction, goNext/goPrev) is\n * delegated to the reusable useCursorPagination hook; this hook just fetches the\n * page described by its `request` and exposes the result.\n */\nexport function useArticles(limit = 5) {\n  const [state, setState] = useState<ArticlesState>({ status: \"loading\" });\n  const [isFetching, setIsFetching] = useState(true);\n  // Skip the scroll-to-top on the very first load (already at the top).\n  const isInitialLoad = useRef(true);\n\n  const pageInfo = state.status === \"ready\" ? state.pageInfo : null;\n  const { request, goNext, goPrev } = useCursorPagination(pageInfo);\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    const controller = new AbortController();\n    setIsFetching(true);\n\n    async function load() {\n      const params = new URLSearchParams({ limit: String(limit) });\n      if (request.cursor) {\n        params.set(\"cursor\", request.cursor);\n        params.set(\"direction\", request.direction);\n      }\n\n      try {\n        const res = await fetch(`/api/articles?${params.toString()}`, {\n          signal: controller.signal,\n        });\n        if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`Request failed: ${res.status}`);\n        const body = (await res.json()) as Paginated<Article>;\n        setState({\n          status: \"ready\",\n          articles: body.data,\n          pageInfo: body.pageInfo,\n        });\n        // On a page change (not the first load), scroll back to the top so the\n        // new page starts at article one.\n        if (isInitialLoad.current) {\n          isInitialLoad.current = false;\n        } else {\n          window.scrollTo({ top: 0, behavior: \"smooth\" });\n        }\n      } catch (err) {\n        if (controller.signal.aborted) return;\n        setState({\n          status: \"error\",\n          message: err instanceof Error ? err.message : \"Unknown error\",\n        });\n      } finally {\n        if (!controller.signal.aborted) setIsFetching(false);\n      }\n    }\n\n    void load();\n    return () => controller.abort();\n  }, [request, limit]);\n\n  return { state, isFetching, goNext, goPrev };\n}\n"
}

## 🤖 Assistant  
<sub>2026-07-25T16:08:45.741Z</sub>

The plan is written. Here's the shape of it:

## Approach
A **single canonical query string** is the source of truth. The visual builder serializes to it, the advanced text box types it directly, and the API parses it — one grammar, one parser.

**Parser (`@carma/shared`, reused):** tokenizer → recursive-descent parser → AST, with precedence `OR < AND < NOT`. Case-sensitivity falls out naturally (only uppercase `AND`/`OR`/`NOT` are operators). Terms are restricted to Unicode word chars — which supports Arabic/Chinese *and* is what makes wildcard compilation injection-safe.

**Compiler (API):** AST → a **parameterized** `tsquery` built from combinators — `plainto_tsquery`/`phraseto_tsquery`/`to_tsquery(term‖':*')` leaves joined with `&&`/`||`/`!!`. User text is never string-interpolated into SQL, and it rides the existing `GIN(search_vector)` index. Search is a **boolean filter** (no ranking), so it keeps the keyset `(published_at, id)` order and composes with the pagination you already have — including threading the predicate through the `hasNext`/`hasPrev` probes so the flags stay correct.

**Frontend:** a `SearchBar` with Builder | Advanced modes — react-querybuilder (custom `formatQuery` → canonical string, live preview) and a validated text box (via the shared parser). New search resets to page 1.

**Tests (vitest):** parser units (precedence, nesting, phrases, wildcards, case-sensitivity, error cases), compiler units (assert generated SQL + bound params), and DB-integration tests proving real `@@` matches (e.g. `renew*` → the Renewable article, `AND NOT startup*` exclusion).

Two things I flagged as out-of-scope with reasoning: relevance ranking (conflicts with keyset cursors) and the FTS+keyset scaling nuance.

## Approved Plan:
# Plan: Boolean full-text search (parser → tsquery) + query-builder UI

## Context

The app can list/paginate articles but can't yet **search** them. We need boolean
search over `headline`/`body` supporting: `AND` / `OR` / `AND NOT` (**case-
sensitive** — lowercase `and`/`or`/`not` are plain terms), **nesting**
(`a AND (b OR c)`), **phrases** (`"media intelligence"`), and **prefix wildcards**
(`renew*` → matches "renewable"/"renewables"). This is the design already sketched
in `README.md` ("hand-rolled parser → Postgres `to_tsquery`"), now implemented and
tested.

Locked-in decisions: search is an optional **`?q=` on the existing
`GET /api/articles`** (composes with the keyset pagination already built); the
**parser lives in `@carma/shared`** (reused by the API to compile, and by the web
to validate typed input); tests are **unit + DB-integration**.

**Phasing (this pass):** build the **backend** (parser, compiler, API, tests) and
the **frontend advanced mode only** — a validated typed query box — so the whole
search path works end-to-end. **`react-querybuilder` (the visual builder) is
deferred** to a follow-up and may be dropped under time pressure; the design keeps
the canonical query string as the contract so the builder can slot in later
(builder→string) without touching the backend.

The `search_vector tsvector` column + `GIN` index already exist — this feature is
the query language and UI on top of them; no schema change.

## The canonical query language (grammar)

One string is the single source of truth (builder serializes to it; advanced mode
types it; the API parses it). Grammar, precedence `OR < AND < NOT < primary`:

```
expr    := orExpr
orExpr  := andExpr ( 'OR'  andExpr )*
andExpr := notExpr ( 'AND' notExpr )*
notExpr := 'NOT' notExpr | primary
primary := '(' expr ')' | phrase | term
phrase  := '"' ... '"'          # → phraseto_tsquery
term    := WORD | WORD '*'      # WORD* → prefix wildcard
```

- `AND` / `OR` / `NOT` are operators **only when uppercase**; `and`/`or`/`not`
  tokenize as terms. `AND NOT` = `AND` followed by unary `NOT`.
- `WORD` = Unicode letters/digits (`\p{L}\p{N}_`, `u` flag) so Arabic/Chinese terms
  work; this charset restriction is also what makes wildcard compilation injection-
  safe (see below). Any other char is a syntax error.
- Empty/whitespace input parses to `null` (= "no search filter"); malformed input
  throws `ParseError` (message + position).

## Parser — `packages/shared/src/search/` (shared, unit-tested)

- `ast.ts` — `QueryNode` union: `{type:'term',value}` `{type:'phrase',value}`
  `{type:'prefix',value}` `{type:'and',left,right}` `{type:'or',left,right}`
  `{type:'not',operand}`.
- `tokenizer.ts` — string → tokens (`AND|OR|NOT|(|)|PHRASE|TERM|PREFIX`), tracking
  positions; case-sensitive keyword recognition.
- `parser.ts` — recursive-descent per the grammar → `QueryNode`; `parseQuery(input):
  QueryNode | null`; `class ParseError extends Error { position }`.
- Re-export `parseQuery`, `ParseError`, and the AST types from
  `packages/shared/src/index.ts` so both apps get them from `@carma/shared`.

## Compiler — `apps/api/src/search/compile.ts` (API, unit-tested)

`compileToTsquery(node): SQL` maps the AST to a **parameterized** drizzle `sql`
expression built from `tsquery` combinators — user text never enters SQL as text:

- `term`   → `plainto_tsquery('simple', $value)`
- `phrase` → `phraseto_tsquery('simple', $value)`  (yields `w1 <-> w2`)
- `prefix` → `to_tsquery('simple', $ (value + ':*'))`  (value is `\w+`-validated, so
  concatenating `:*` is safe)
- `and`→`(L && R)`  `or`→`(L || R)`  `not`→`(!! X)`  (tsquery operators)

Predicate applied in the route: `sql\`${articles.searchVector} @@ ${compiled}\``.
This rides the existing `GIN(search_vector)` index. **No relevance ranking** — search
is a boolean *filter*; results stay ordered by the keyset `(published_at, id)` so it
composes with the existing pagination.

## API integration — `apps/api/src/routes/articles.ts`

- Read `q`; if present & non-empty → `parseQuery` (catch `ParseError` → **400**
  `ApiError`) → `compileToTsquery` → a `searchPredicate` SQL.
- Combine `searchPredicate` (AND) with the existing keyset `where` on the **data
  query and both `hasOlder`/`hasNewer` existence probes** — otherwise the
  next/prev flags would ignore the filter. Refactor the probes to accept an extra
  predicate.
- Everything else (limit, cursor, direction, `NULLS LAST` ordering, join to
  `sources`) is unchanged.

## Frontend — `apps/web` (advanced mode only this pass)

- `components/SearchBar.tsx` — a **validated typed query box** (no new deps):
  - free-form text input validated live via `parseQuery` from `@carma/shared`
    (inline error message + character position); Search disabled while invalid.
  - Submit lifts the query string up; a "Clear" button resets to the unfiltered
    feed. A tiny hint lists the supported syntax (`AND` `OR` `AND NOT` `( )`
    `"phrase"` `term*`).
- `App.tsx` holds `q` state, renders `<SearchBar onSearch={setQ} />`, passes `q` to
  the hook.
- `hooks/useArticles.ts` — accept `q`; include it in the fetch params.
- `hooks/useCursorPagination.ts` — accept a `resetKey` (pass `q`); when it changes,
  reset `request` to the first page (new search starts at page 1).

**Deferred (follow-up, optional):** a **Builder** mode using `react-querybuilder`
(combinators `AND`/`OR`, group `not`→`NOT`, a `text` field whose operators map to
term/phrase/prefix), serialized to the canonical string via a custom `formatQuery`
and handed one-way into this text box. Slots in behind the same `onSearch` string
contract with no backend change.

## Testing — vitest (unit) + DB integration

- Add `vitest` to `@carma/shared` and `@carma/api`; `test` script in each; root
  `test` → `yarn workspaces foreach -Ap run test`.
- **Parser unit** (`packages/shared/src/search/*.test.ts`): precedence &
  associativity, nesting, phrases, prefix wildcards, **case-sensitivity**
  (`AND` op vs `and` term), unicode terms, and errors (unbalanced parens, dangling
  operator, unterminated phrase, stray `*`, empty phrase).
- **Compiler unit** (`apps/api/src/search/compile.test.ts`): assert generated SQL +
  params via drizzle's `PgDialect().sqlToQuery(...)` — correct `plainto_/phraseto_/
  :*` leaves and `&& || !!` structure, all values bound as parameters.
- **DB integration** (`apps/api/src/search/search.integration.test.ts`,
  `describe.skipIf(!DATABASE_URL)`): against seeded data assert real `@@` matches —
  e.g. `renew*` → article 5; `"oil prices"` → article 1; `AI AND NOT startup*`
  includes the AI-regulation article but excludes the healthcare-startup one;
  `(oil OR renewable) AND NOT nuclear` behaves. Uses the existing `db` client.

## Files

- **New** `packages/shared/src/search/{ast,tokenizer,parser}.ts` (+ `*.test.ts`);
  re-export from `packages/shared/src/index.ts`.
- **New** `apps/api/src/search/compile.ts` (+ `compile.test.ts`,
  `search.integration.test.ts`).
- **Edit** `apps/api/src/routes/articles.ts` (q → predicate; probes take a filter).
- **New** `apps/web/src/components/SearchBar.tsx` (validated text box); **edit**
  `App.tsx`, `hooks/useArticles.ts`, `hooks/useCursorPagination.ts`.
- **Edit** `package.json` (root + shared + api): add `vitest` + `test` scripts.
  (No `react-querybuilder` this pass — deferred.)
- **Edit** `README.md`: API surface (`?q=` on `/api/articles`); the search-approach
  section already documents the parser/compile design.

## Verification

1. `yarn test` — parser + compiler units green; DB-integration green against the
   docker Postgres.
2. `yarn typecheck` clean; web build clean.
3. `docker compose up`, then curl each capability:
   - phrase `?q="oil prices"`, wildcard `?q=renew*`, boolean
     `?q=AI AND NOT startup*`, nesting `?q=(oil OR renewable) AND NOT nuclear`,
     case-sensitivity `?q=oil and gas` (treats `and` as a term), malformed
     `?q=oil AND` → **400**.
   - search **+ pagination**: `?q=...&limit=2` then follow `cursor`/`direction`,
     confirming `hasNext`/`hasPrev` respect the filter.
4. UI at `http://localhost:5173`: type queries in the advanced box — valid ones
   (`renew*`, `"oil prices"`, `AI AND NOT startup*`) return results; malformed ones
   show inline validation and disable Search; a new search resets to page 1; Clear
   restores the full feed.

## Out of scope (noted for later)

- **`react-querybuilder` visual builder** — deferred to a follow-up (may be dropped
  under time pressure); slots in behind the canonical-string `onSearch` contract.
- Relevance ranking (`ts_rank`) — conflicts with keyset ordering; would need a
  rank-based cursor. Search stays a recency-ordered filter for now.
- Combining FTS with keyset pagination is a known scaling nuance (GIN filter vs
  keyset index); correct now, revisit strategy if search-heavy load grows.
- Filters (source/language/date) aren't part of this pass; the `q` predicate is
  written to slot alongside them when they land.

  "content": "/** A lexical token with its start position in the source string. */\nexport interface Token {\n  type: \"AND\" | \"OR\" | \"NOT\" | \"LPAREN\" | \"RPAREN\" | \"PHRASE\" | \"TERM\" | \"PREFIX\";\n  /** For PHRASE/TERM/PREFIX: the text value. For operators/parens: the literal. */\n  value: string;\n  /** 0-based index into the input where this token starts. */\n  position: number;\n}\n\n/** Raised on malformed input; `position` points at the offending character. */\nexport class ParseError extends Error {\n  readonly position: number;\n  constructor(message: string, position: number) {\n    super(message);\n    this.name = \"ParseError\";\n    this.position = position;\n  }\n}\n\n// A \"word\" character: Unicode letters, digits, and underscore. Restricting\n// terms to this set is what lets the compiler safely append `:*` for wildcards\n// and keeps `tsquery` meta-characters (& | ! : < >) out of user input.\nconst WORD_CHAR = /[\\p{L}\\p{N}_]/u;\n\nconst KEYWORDS = new Set([\"AND\", \"OR\", \"NOT\"]);\n\n/**\n * Turn a query string into tokens. Uppercase AND/OR/NOT are operators; any\n * other casing is an ordinary term. A word immediately followed by `*` is a\n * prefix (wildcard) token.\n */\nexport function tokenize(input: string): Token[] {\n  const tokens: Token[] = [];\n  let i = 0;\n\n  while (i < input.length) {\n    const ch = input[i]!;\n\n    if (/\\s/.test(ch)) {\n      i += 1;\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    if (ch === \"(\") {\n      tokens.push({ type: \"LPAREN\", value: \"(\", position: i });\n      i += 1;\n      continue;\n    }\n    if (ch === \")\") {\n      tokens.push({ type: \"RPAREN\", value: \")\", position: i });\n      i += 1;\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    if (ch === '\"') {\n      const start = i;\n      i += 1;\n      let value = \"\";\n      while (i < input.length && input[i] !== '\"') {\n        value += input[i];\n        i += 1;\n      }\n      if (i >= input.length) {\n        throw new ParseError(\"Unterminated phrase (missing closing quote)\", start);\n      }\n      i += 1; // consume closing quote\n      if (value.trim().length === 0) {\n        throw new ParseError(\"Empty phrase\", start);\n      }\n      tokens.push({ type: \"PHRASE\", value, position: start });\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    if (WORD_CHAR.test(ch)) {\n      const start = i;\n      let word = \"\";\n      while (i < input.length && WORD_CHAR.test(input[i]!)) {\n        word += input[i];\n        i += 1;\n      }\n      // A trailing '*' makes it a prefix (wildcard) token.\n      if (input[i] === \"*\") {\n        i += 1;\n        tokens.push({ type: \"PREFIX\", value: word, position: start });\n        continue;\n      }\n      if (KEYWORDS.has(word)) {\n        tokens.push({ type: word as \"AND\" | \"OR\" | \"NOT\", value: word, position: start });\n      } else {\n        tokens.push({ type: \"TERM\", value: word, position: start });\n      }\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    if (ch === \"*\") {\n      throw new ParseError(\"Unexpected '*' (wildcards must follow a term)\", i);\n    }\n\n    throw new ParseError(`Unexpected character '${ch}'`, i);\n  }\n\n  return tokens;\n}\n"

Throws\n * `ParseError` (with a position) on malformed input.\n */\nexport function parseQuery(input: string): QueryNode | null {\n  const tokens = tokenize(input);\n  if (tokens.length === 0) return null;\n\n  let pos = 0;\n  const peek = (): Token | undefined => tokens[pos];\n  const eof = (): number => input.length;\n\n  function parseOr(): QueryNode {\n    let left = parseAnd();\n    while (peek()?.type === \"OR\") {\n      pos += 1;\n      const right = parseAnd();\n      left = { type: \"or\", left, right };\n    }\n    return left;\n  }\n\n  function parseAnd(): QueryNode {\n    let left = parseNot();\n    for (;;) {\n      const t = peek();\n      if (t?.type === \"AND\") {\n        pos += 1;\n        left = { type: \"and\", left, right: parseNot() };\n      } else if (t && PRIMARY_START.has(t.type)) {\n        // Implicit AND between adjacent operands.\n        left = { type: \"and\", left, right: parseNot() };\n      } else {\n        return left;\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  function parseNot(): QueryNode {\n    if (peek()?.type === \"NOT\") {\n      pos += 1;\n      return { type: \"not\", operand: parseNot() };\n    }\n    return parsePrimary();\n  }\n\n  function parsePrimary(): QueryNode {\n    const t = peek();\n    if (!t) {\n      throw new ParseError(\"Unexpected end of query\", eof());\n    }\n    switch (t.type) {\n      case \"LPAREN\": {\n        pos += 1;\n        const inner = parseOr();\n        const close = peek();\n        if (close?.type !== \"RPAREN\") {\n          throw new ParseError(\"Expected ')'\", close?.position ?? eof());\n        }\n        pos += 1;\n        return inner;\n      }\n      case \"PHRASE\":\n        pos += 1;\n        return { type: \"phrase\", value: t.value };\n      case \"TERM\":\n        pos += 1;\n        return { type: \"term\", value: t.value };\n      case \"PREFIX\":\n        pos += 1;\n        return { type: \"prefix\", value: t.value };\n      default:\n        throw new ParseError(`Unexpected '${t.value}'`, t.position);\n    }\n  }\n\n  const node = parseOr();\n  const trailing = peek();\n  if (trailing) {\n    throw new ParseError(`Unexpected '${trailing.value}'`, trailing.position);\n  }\n  return node;\n}\n"

{
  "file_path": "/Users/garythrels/Development/personal/carma/apps/api/src/search/compile.ts",
  "content": "import type { QueryNode } from \"@carma/shared\";\nimport { sql, type SQL } from \"drizzle-orm\";\n\n// Text-search configuration. 'simple' (no stemming/stopwords) so multilingual\n// content matches predictably and prefix wildcards behave — matches the config\n// used to build articles.search_vector.\nconst CONFIG = \"simple\";\n\n/**\n * Compile a parsed query AST into a Postgres `tsquery` SQL expression.\n *\n * Leaves are built with `plainto_tsquery` / `phraseto_tsquery` / `to_tsquery`\n * and every user value is passed as a **bound parameter** — user text never\n * becomes SQL syntax. Nodes combine with the tsquery operators `&&` (and),\n * `||` (or) and `!!` (not). The result is meant to be used as:\n *\n *   sql`${articles.searchVector} @@ ${compileToTsquery(node)}`\n */\nexport function compileToTsquery(node: QueryNode): SQL {\n  switch (node.type) {\n    case \"term\":\n      return sql`plainto_tsquery(${CONFIG}, ${node.value})`;\n    case \"phrase\":\n      return sql`phraseto_tsquery(${CONFIG}, ${node.value})`;\n    case \"prefix\":\n      // node.value is `[\\p{L}\\p{N}_]+` (enforced by the parser), so appending\n      // ':*' to form a prefix query is safe. The whole string is still bound.\n      return sql`to_tsquery(${CONFIG}, ${node.value + \":*\"})`;\n    case \"and\":\n      return sql`(${compileToTsquery(node.left)} && ${compileToTsquery(node.right)})`;\n    case \"or\":\n      return sql`(${compileToTsquery(node.left)} || ${compileToTsquery(node.right)})`;\n    case \"not\":\n      return sql`(!! ${compileToTsquery(node.operand)})`;\n  }\n}\n"
}

...)\", () => {\n    const { sql, params } = render(\"renewable AND NOT nuclear\");\n    expect(sql).toBe(\n      \"(plainto_tsquery($1, $2) && (!! plainto_tsquery($3, $4)))\",\n    );\n    expect(params).toEqual([\"simple\", \"renewable\", \"simple\", \"nuclear\"]);\n  });\n\n  it(\"nested groups compile with correct structure and params\", () => {\n    const { sql, params } = render('\"oil prices\" AND (geopolitical OR renew*)');\n    expect(sql).toBe(\n      \"(phraseto_tsquery($1, $2) && (plainto_tsquery($3, $4) || to_tsquery($5, $6)))\",\n    );\n    expect(params).toEqual([\n      \"simple\",\n      \"oil prices\",\n      \"simple\",\n      \"geopolitical\",\n      \"simple\",\n      \"renew:*\",\n    ]);\n  });\n});\n\ndescribe(\"compileToTsquery — safety\", () => {\n  it(\"keeps user values as parameters, not inlined SQL\", () => {\n    // The parser rejects tsquery metacharacters, but even ordinary values must\n    // travel as bound params — never interpolated into the SQL text.\n    const { sql, params } = render(\"oil\");\n    expect(sql).not.toContain(\"oil\");\n    expect(params).toContain(\"oil\");\n  });\n});\n"

  "content": "import { PageInfo } from \"@carma/shared\";\nimport { useCallback, useRef, useState } from \"react\";\n\n/** What page to request: the current page's cursor + which way to move from it. */\nexport interface CursorRequest {\n  cursor: string | null;\n  direction: \"next\" | \"prev\";\n}\n\nconst FIRST_PAGE: CursorRequest = { cursor: null, direction: \"next\" };\n\n/**\n * Reusable keyset-pagination navigation. Owns the `request` (cursor + direction)\n * that a data hook feeds into its fetch, and derives `goNext`/`goPrev` from the\n * latest `PageInfo`. Not tied to any particular resource.\n *\n * Pass `resetKey` (e.g. the current search query) to snap back to the first page\n * whenever it changes — the reset happens during render so the data hook makes a\n * single fetch, not one for the stale cursor and another for the reset.\n */\nexport function useCursorPagination(\n  pageInfo: PageInfo | null,\n  resetKey?: unknown,\n) {\n  const [request, setRequest] = useState<CursorRequest>(FIRST_PAGE);\n\n  // Reset to page one when resetKey changes (render-time, guarded — the React\n  // \"adjusting state on prop change\" pattern).\n  const prevResetKey = useRef(resetKey);\n  if (prevResetKey.current !== resetKey) {\n    prevResetKey.current = resetKey;\n    setRequest(FIRST_PAGE);\n  }\n\n  // Keep the latest pageInfo in a ref so goNext/goPrev stay referentially stable\n  // while always reading current values.\n  const pageInfoRef = useRef<PageInfo | null>(pageInfo);\n  pageInfoRef.current = pageInfo;\n\n  const goNext = useCallback(() => {\n    const pi = pageInfoRef.current;\n    if (pi?.hasNext && pi.cursor) {\n      setRequest({ cursor: pi.cursor, direction: \"next\" });\n    }\n  }, []);\n\n  const goPrev = useCallback(() => {\n    const pi = pageInfoRef.current;\n    if (pi?.hasPrev && pi.cursor) {\n      setRequest({ cursor: pi.cursor, direction: \"prev\" });\n    }\n  }, []);\n\n  return {\n    request,\n    goNext,\n    goPrev,\n    canNext: pageInfo?.hasNext ?? false,\n    canPrev: pageInfo?.hasPrev ?? false,\n  };\n}\n"
}

Navigation is\n * delegated to useCursorPagination; passing `q` as its reset key snaps back to\n * page one whenever the search changes.\n */\nexport function useArticles(q = \"\", limit = 5) {\n  const [state, setState] = useState<ArticlesState>({ status: \"loading\" });\n  const [isFetching, setIsFetching] = useState(true);\n  // Skip the scroll-to-top on the very first load (already at the top).\n  const isInitialLoad = useRef(true);\n\n  const pageInfo = state.status === \"ready\" ? state.pageInfo : null;\n  const { request, goNext, goPrev } = useCursorPagination(pageInfo, q);\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    const controller = new AbortController();\n    setIsFetching(true);\n\n    async function load() {\n      const params = new URLSearchParams({ limit: String(limit) });\n      if (request.cursor) {\n        params.set(\"cursor\", request.cursor);\n        params.set(\"direction\", request.direction);\n      }\n      const trimmed = q.trim();\n      if (trimmed) params.set(\"q\", trimmed);\n\n      try {\n        const res = await fetch(`/api/articles?${params.toString()}`, {\n          signal: controller.signal,\n        });\n        if (!res.ok) {\n          let message = `Request failed: ${res.status}`;\n          try {\n            const body = (await res.json()) as ApiError;\n            if (body?.error) message = body.error;\n          } catch {\n            /* keep the status-based message */\n          }\n          throw new Error(message);\n        }\n        const body = (await res.json()) as Paginated<Article>;\n        setState({\n          status: \"ready\",\n          articles: body.data,\n          pageInfo: body.pageInfo,\n        });\n        // On a page/search change (not the first load), scroll back to the top.\n        if (isInitialLoad.current) {\n          isInitialLoad.current = false;\n        } else {\n          window.scrollTo({ top: 0, behavior: \"smooth\" });\n        }\n      } catch (err) {\n        if (controller.signal.aborted) return;\n        setState({\n          status: \"error\",\n          message: err instanceof Error ? err.message : \"Unknown error\",\n        });\n      } finally {\n        if (!controller.signal.aborted) setIsFetching(false);\n      }\n    }\n\n    void load();\n    return () => controller.abort();\n  }, [request, limit, q]);\n\n  return { state, isFetching, goNext, goPrev };\n}\n"
}

The visual query builder will\n * later feed this same string contract.\n */\nexport function SearchBar({ onSearch }: Props) {\n  const [text, setText] = useState(\"\");\n  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);\n\n  /** Validate `value`; set/clear the error and return whether it's valid. */\n  function validate(value: string): boolean {\n    try {\n      parseQuery(value); // empty/whitespace -> null (valid, no filter)\n      setError(null);\n      return true;\n    } catch (err) {\n      setError(\n        err instanceof ParseError\n          ? `${err.message} (position ${err.position + 1})`\n          : \"Invalid query\",\n      );\n      return false;\n    }\n  }\n\n  function handleChange(value: string) {\n    setText(value);\n    validate(value);\n  }\n\n  function handleSubmit(e: FormEvent) {\n    e.preventDefault();\n    if (validate(text)) onSearch(text.trim());\n  }\n\n  function handleClear() {\n    setText(\"\");\n    setError(null);\n    onSearch(\"\");\n  }\n\n  const invalid = error !== null;\n\n  return (\n    <form className=\"search\" onSubmit={handleSubmit}>\n      <div className=\"search-row\">\n        <input\n          type=\"text\"\n          className={invalid ? \"search-input invalid\" : \"search-input\"}\n          placeholder={'Search… e.g.  \"oil prices\" AND renew*'}\n          value={text}\n          onChange={(e) => handleChange(e.target.value)}\n          aria-invalid={invalid}\n          aria-label=\"Search query\"\n        />\n        <button type=\"submit\" disabled={invalid}>\n          Search\n        </button>\n        <button type=\"button\" onClick={handleClear} disabled={text === \"\"}>\n          Clear\n        </button>\n      </div>\n      {invalid ? (\n        <p className=\"search-error\">{error}</p>\n      ) : (\n        <p className=\"search-hint\">\n          <code>AND</code> <code>OR</code> <code>AND NOT</code> · groups{\" \"}\n          <code>( )</code> · phrase <code>\"…\"</code> · wildcard <code>term*</code>\n        </p>\n      )}\n    </form>\n  );\n}\n"

Everything's verified. The backend + advanced search mode are complete and fully tested. Teardown done (volume kept).

## What shipped

**Boolean query language** (`@carma/shared/src/search/`) — reused by API + web:
- Tokenizer + recursive-descent parser → AST. Precedence `OR < AND < NOT`, nesting, phrases, prefix wildcards, **case-sensitive** operators (lowercase `and`/`or`/`not` are terms), **implicit AND** for adjacency, Unicode terms, and `ParseError` with a position.

**Compiler** (`apps/api/src/search/compile.ts`):
- AST → **parameterized** `tsquery` from `plainto_tsquery`/`phraseto_tsquery`/`to_tsquery(…':*')` leaves joined with `&&`/`||`/`!!`. User text is never interpolated into SQL; it rides the existing `GIN(search_vector)` index.

**API** (`GET /api/articles?q=`):
- Optional `q` parsed (400 on `ParseError`) → predicate ANDed into the keyset query **and** both `hasNext`/`hasPrev` probes, so search composes with the pagination you already have.

**Frontend advanced mode**:
- `SearchBar` — typed query box with **live validation** via the shared parser (inline error + position), disabled Search when invalid, Clear, and a syntax hint. `useArticles(q)` threads the query; `useCursorPagination(pageInfo, q)` resets to page 1 on a new search (render-time reset → single fetch).

**Tests** (vitest): **23 parser** + **8 compiler** unit tests (green, DB-free) and **7 DB-integration** tests proving real `@@` matches. Root `yarn test` runs units; integration self-skips without `DATABASE_URL`.

## Verified end-to-end
Against the live stack — phrase (`"oil prices"`→[1], reversed→[]), wildcard (`renew*`→[5]), `AI AND NOT startup*`→[2,3], nesting→[1,5], lowercase-`and`-as-term→[], malformed→**400**, and **search + pagination** round-tripping — plus the same through the Vite proxy the browser uses (`"oil prices" OR renew*`→[1,5]).

NULLS LAST/FIRST is\n// required so the planner uses the index instead of sorting (see README).\nconst ORDER_DESC = sql`${articles.publishedAt} DESC NULLS LAST, ${articles.id} DESC NULLS LAST`;\nconst ORDER_ASC = sql`${articles.publishedAt} ASC NULLS FIRST, ${articles.id} ASC NULLS FIRST`;\n\n/** Keyset predicate: older than the anchor for `next`, newer for `prev`. */\nfunction keysetPredicate(anchor: KeysetAnchor, direction: \"next\" | \"prev\"): SQL {\n  return direction === \"prev\"\n    ? sql`(${articles.publishedAt}, ${articles.id}) > (${anchor.publishedAt}, ${anchor.id})`\n    : sql`(${articles.publishedAt}, ${articles.id}) < (${anchor.publishedAt}, ${anchor.id})`;\n}\n\n/** Does any row exist beyond `anchor` (older/newer), honouring the filter? */\nasync function existsBeyond(\n  anchor: KeysetAnchor,\n  side: \"older\" | \"newer\",\n  filter: SQL | undefined,\n): Promise<boolean> {\n  const cmp =\n    side === \"older\"\n      ? sql`(${articles.publishedAt}, ${articles.id}) < (${anchor.publishedAt}, ${anchor.id})`\n      : sql`(${articles.publishedAt}, ${articles.id}) > (${anchor.publishedAt}, ${anchor.id})`;\n  const rows = await db\n    .select({ one: sql`1` })\n    .from(articles)\n    .where(and(cmp, filter))\n    .limit(1);\n  return rows.length > 0;\n}\n\n/**\n * Fetch one keyset page of articles (newest-first) plus its navigation flags.\n * `hasNext`/`hasPrev` are computed with index-only existence probes that also\n * apply the filter, so they stay correct under search and either direction.\n */\nexport async function findArticlesPage({\n  limit,\n  direction,\n  anchor,\n  filter,\n}: FindArticlesPageParams): Promise<ArticlesPage> {\n  const keyset = anchor ? keysetPredicate(anchor, direction) : undefined;\n  const where = and(keyset, filter);\n\n  const query = db\n    .select({\n      id: articles.id,\n      headline: articles.headline,\n      body: articles.body,\n      source: sources.name,\n      publishedAt: articles.publishedAt,\n      createdAt: articles.createdAt,\n    })\n    .from(articles)\n    .innerJoin(sources, eq(articles.sourceId, sources.id))\n    .$dynamic();\n\n  if (where) query.where(where);\n  const rows = await query\n    .orderBy(direction === \"prev\" ? ORDER_ASC : ORDER_DESC)\n    .limit(limit);\n  // Backward pages are scanned ascending (closest-first); flip to newest-first.\n  if (direction === \"prev\") rows.reverse();\n\n  if (rows.length === 0) {\n    return { rows: [], hasNext: false, hasPrev: false };\n  }\n\n  const first = rows[0]!;\n  const last = rows[rows.length - 1]!;\n  const [hasPrev, hasNext] = await Promise.all([\n    existsBeyond({ publishedAt: first.publishedAt, id: first.id }, \"newer\", filter),\n    existsBeyond({ publishedAt: last.publishedAt, id: last.id }, \"older\", filter),\n  ]);\n\n  return { rows, hasNext, hasPrev };\n}\n"

\"prev\" : \"next\";\n  const q = typeof req.query.q === \"string\" ? req.query.q : undefined;\n  const cursorToken =\n    typeof req.query.cursor === \"string\" && req.query.cursor.length > 0\n      ? req.query.cursor\n      : undefined;\n\n  // Build filters (malformed search query → 400).\n  let filter;\n  try {\n    filter = buildArticleFilters({ q });\n  } catch (err) {\n    if (err instanceof ParseError) return badRequest(res, err.message);\n    throw err;\n  }\n\n  // Decode the cursor token into the keyset anchor for this direction (→ 400).\n  let anchor: KeysetAnchor | undefined;\n  if (cursorToken) {\n    try {\n      const cursor = decodeCursor(cursorToken);\n      const edge = direction === \"prev\" ? <sub>2026-07-25T17:16:18.783Z</sub>

The articles route is refactored into a clean, feature-based module following SOLID/DDD separation.

## New structure
```
apps/api/src/features/articles/
├── articles.router.ts      # HTTP only: parse request → filters → repository → mapper → respond
├── articles.repository.ts  # all data access: keyset page query + existence probes
├── articles.filters.ts     # request inputs → SQL predicates (search now; source/lang/date later)
└── articles.mapper.ts      # DB row → shared Article DTO
```
`src/routes/` is gone. The generic, cross-feature helpers stayed put: `lib/cursor.ts` (opaque token encode/decode) and `search/compile.ts` (query-language → tsquery).

## How it maps to SOLID
- **Single responsibility** — each file does exactly one thing; the router is now thin orchestration.
- **Open/closed** — `buildArticleFilters` is built to grow: adding source/language/date filters is a new private builder AND-combined in one place, no router changes.
- **Dependency direction** — only the **repository** touches the DB; router→(filters, repository, mapper, cursor) with no cycles. The mapper depends on the repository's `ArticleListRow` contract, not the other way around.

## Also fixed (was blocking the build)
Your in-progress shared reorg had moved types out of `index.ts` but left `types/index.ts` **empty (0 bytes)** — so `Article`/`Paginated`/etc. were defined nowhere and every workspace failed typecheck. Since your `index.ts` already re-exports `export type * from "./types"`, I **completed** that move by populating `types/index.ts` with the definitions (not a revert — it finishes the direction you started). You've since tweaked a comment there, so it's in your hands now.

## Verified
- `yarn typecheck` clean across all workspaces; **23 parser + 8 compiler** unit tests green.
- Runtime smoke test of the rewired endpoint: default list `[1-5]` → page 2 `[6-10]`, search `"oil prices" OR renew*` → `[1,5]`, malformed `q` → **400**, bad cursor → **400**. Behavior identical to before the refactor.

Teardown done (volume kept). The `react-querybuilder` visual builder is still the open follow-up whenever you want it.

  "file_path": "/Users/garythrels/Development/personal/carma/apps/api/src/features/articles/articles.pagination.ts",
  "content": "import { sql, type SQL } from \"drizzle-orm\";\nimport type { PageInfo } from \"@carma/shared\";\nimport { articles } from \"../../db/schema.js\";\nimport { decodeCursor, encodeCursor } from \"../../lib/cursor.js\";\n\n/**\n * Keyset (cursor) pagination for the article feed, ordered `(published_at DESC,\n * id DESC)`. Everything specific to *how we page* lives here: request parsing,\n * index-matching ordering, keyset predicates, and cursor-token ↔ position\n * translation. The repository runs queries with these; the router speaks HTTP.\n */\n\nexport type Direction = \"next\" | \"prev\";\n\n/** A keyset position — the `(published_at, id)` pair a page is anchored on. */\nexport interface KeysetAnchor {\n  publishedAt: Date;\n  id: number;\n}\n\nexport const DEFAULT_LIMIT = 5;\nexport const MAX_LIMIT = 50;\n\nexport function parseLimit(raw: unknown): number {\n  const n = Number(raw);\n  if (Number.isInteger(n) && n > 0) return Math.min(n, MAX_LIMIT);\n  return DEFAULT_LIMIT;\n}\n\nexport function parseDirection(raw: unknown): Direction {\n  return raw === \"prev\" ? \"prev\" : \"next\";\n}\n\n// Ordering matches the articles_published_at_id_idx index. NULLS LAST/FIRST is\n// required so the planner uses the index instead of sorting (see README).\nconst ORDER_DESC = sql`${articles.publishedAt} DESC NULLS LAST, ${articles.id} DESC NULLS LAST`;\nconst ORDER_ASC = sql`${articles.publishedAt} ASC NULLS FIRST, ${articles.id} ASC NULLS FIRST`;\n\n/** Feed order for a direction; backward pages scan ascending, then get reversed. */\nexport function orderFor(direction: Direction): SQL {\n  return direction === \"prev\" ? ORDER_ASC : ORDER_DESC;\n}\n\n/** Rows strictly older than the anchor. */\nexport function olderThan(a: KeysetAnchor): SQL {\n  return sql`(${articles.publishedAt}, ${articles.id}) < (${a.publishedAt}, ${a.id})`;\n}\n\n/** Rows strictly newer than the anchor. */\nexport function newerThan(a: KeysetAnchor): SQL {\n  return sql`(${articles.publishedAt}, ${articles.id}) > (${a.publishedAt}, ${a.id})`;\n}\n\n/** Keyset predicate to page from an anchor: older for `next`, newer for `prev`. */\nexport function keysetPredicate(a: KeysetAnchor, direction: Direction): SQL {\n  return direction === \"prev\" ? newerThan(a) : olderThan(a);\n}\n\n/** Decode a cursor token to the anchor for this direction (throws CursorError). */\nexport function anchorFromCursor(token: string, direction: Direction): KeysetAnchor {\n  const cursor = decodeCursor(token);\n  const edge = direction === \"prev\" ? cursor.f : cursor.l;\n  return { publishedAt: new Date(edge.t), id: edge.i };\n}\n\n/** PageInfo for an empty result. */\nexport const EMPTY_PAGE_INFO: PageInfo = {\n  cursor: null,\n  hasNext: false,\n  hasPrev: false,\n};\n\n/** Build PageInfo (both-edges cursor token + flags) from a page's edges. */\nexport function buildPageInfo(\n  first: KeysetAnchor,\n  last: KeysetAnchor,\n  hasNext: boolean,\n  hasPrev: boolean,\n): PageInfo {\n  const cursor = encodeCursor({\n    f: { t: first.publishedAt.toISOString(), i: first.id },\n    l: { t: last.publishedAt.toISOString(), i: last.id },\n  });\n  return { cursor, hasNext, hasPrev };\n}\n"
}

  "content": "import { and, eq, sql, type SQL } from \"drizzle-orm\";\nimport { db } from \"../../db/index.js\";\nimport { articles, sources } from \"../../db/schema.js\";\nimport {\n  keysetPredicate,\n  newerThan,\n  olderThan,\n  orderFor,\n  type Direction,\n  type KeysetAnchor,\n} from \"./articles.pagination.js\";\n\n/** A joined article row as read from the database (source resolved to a name). */\nexport interface ArticleListRow {\n  id: number;\n  headline: string;\n  body: string;\n  source: string;\n  publishedAt: Date;\n  createdAt: Date;\n}\n\nexport interface FindArticlesPageParams {\n  limit: number;\n  direction: Direction;\n  /** Keyset position to page from; omit for the first page. */\n  anchor?: KeysetAnchor;\n  /** Optional extra predicate (e.g. full-text search) — see articles.filters. */\n  filter?: SQL;\n}\n\nexport interface ArticlesPage {\n  rows: ArticleListRow[];\n  hasNext: boolean;\n  hasPrev: boolean;\n}\n\n/** Does any row satisfy `cmp` (a keyset comparison), honouring the filter? */\nasync function exists(cmp: SQL, filter: SQL | undefined): Promise<boolean> {\n  const rows = await db\n    .select({ one: sql`1` })\n    .from(articles)\n    .where(and(cmp, filter))\n    .limit(1);\n  return rows.length > 0;\n}\n\n/**\n * Fetch one keyset page of articles (newest-first) plus its navigation flags.\n * `hasNext`/`hasPrev` are computed with index-only existence probes that also\n * apply the filter, so they stay correct under search and in either direction.\n */\nexport async function findArticlesPage({\n  limit,\n  direction,\n  anchor,\n  filter,\n}: FindArticlesPageParams): Promise<ArticlesPage> {\n  const where = and(anchor ? keysetPredicate(anchor, direction) : undefined, filter);\n\n  const query = db\n    .select({\n      id: articles.id,\n      headline: articles.headline,\n      body: articles.body,\n      source: sources.name,\n      publishedAt: articles.publishedAt,\n      createdAt: articles.createdAt,\n    })\n    .from(articles)\n    .innerJoin(sources, eq(articles.sourceId, sources.id))\n    .$dynamic();\n\n  if (where) query.where(where);\n  const rows = await query.orderBy(orderFor(direction)).limit(limit);\n  // Backward pages are scanned ascending (closest-first); flip to newest-first.\n  if (direction === \"prev\") rows.reverse();\n\n  if (rows.length === 0) {\n    return { rows: [], hasNext: false, hasPrev: false };\n  }\n\n  const first = rows[0]!;\n  const last = rows[rows.length - 1]!;\n  const [hasPrev, hasNext] = await Promise.all([\n    exists(newerThan({ publishedAt: first.publishedAt, id: first.id }), filter),\n    exists(olderThan({ publishedAt: last.publishedAt, id: last.id }), filter),\n  ]);\n\n  return { rows, hasNext, hasPrev };\n}\n"
}

## Change
New **`apps/api/src/features/articles/articles.pagination.ts`** — the single home for keyset pagination:
- Request parsing: `parseLimit`, `parseDirection`, `DEFAULT_LIMIT`/`MAX_LIMIT`.
- Ordering: index-matching `orderFor(direction)` (the `NULLS LAST/FIRST` SQL).
- Predicates: `olderThan` / `newerThan` / `keysetPredicate`.
- Cursor translation: `anchorFromCursor(token, direction)` and `buildPageInfo(...)` / `EMPTY_PAGE_INFO`.
- Owns the `Direction` and `KeysetAnchor` types.

The other two files got thinner and more focused:
- **`articles.repository.ts`** — now pure data access. It imports the keyset predicates/ordering and just runs queries (the page select + two existence probes collapsed into one `exists(cmp, filter)` helper). No more inline `(published_at, id) < …` SQL or ordering constants.
- **`articles.router.ts`** — no local limit/cursor logic left; it calls `parseLimit`/`parseDirection`/`anchorFromCursor`/`buildPageInfo`. Reads as: parse → filter → repository → map → respond.

## Responsibility boundary now
- **pagination** — *how we page* (keyset SQL + token ↔ position).
- **repository** — *reads the DB*.
- **filters** — *narrowing predicates*.
- **mapper** — *row → DTO*.
- **router** — *HTTP orchestration*.

`lib/cursor.ts` stays the generic token codec that `pagination.ts` builds on.

## Verified
`yarn typecheck` clean across all workspaces; unit tests green (23 parser + 8 compiler). This was a pure internal extraction — same SQL, same cursor token, same endpoint behavior that the smoke test validated last turn — so I didn't spin Docker again. ## 🤖 Assistant  
<sub>2026-07-25T17:35:34.961Z</sub>

Found it. Here's the why and the fix.

## Why it's skipped
The test guards itself with:
```ts
const url = process.env.DATABASE_URL;
describe.skipIf(!url)("boolean search @@ (integration)", () => { … })
```
When you run `yarn test`, **`DATABASE_URL` is not in the process environment** (confirmed: `<unset>`). Your root `.env` *does* have it, but **vitest doesn't load `.env`** (there's no vitest config or dotenv setup), so the variable never reaches the test — `!url` is `true` and the whole block is skipped.

This is intentional: it keeps `yarn test` database-free so it passes in CI without a Postgres. The skip is the guard doing its job, not a bug.

## How to run it
It just needs `DATABASE_URL` set and a migrated+seeded Postgres reachable. Your docker DB is up on `localhost:5432` right now, so:

```bash
DATABASE_URL=postgres://carma:carma@localhost:5432/carma yarn workspace @carma/api test
```

Let me prove that flips it from skipped to running:

## 🤖 Assistant  
<sub>2026-07-25T17:35:59.329Z</sub>

Confirmed — with `DATABASE_URL` set it runs and **all 7 integration tests pass** (15 total, none skipped).

## Summary
- **Why skipped:** `yarn test` runs without `DATABASE_URL` in the env, and vitest doesn't read your `.env`, so the `skipIf(!url)` guard skips the block. By design, so `yarn test` stays green in CI without a database.
- **Prereq to run it:** a Postgres that's **migrated + seeded** (the `beforeAll` throws if it finds fewer than 20 articles). `docker compose up` does this automatically; locally it's `yarn db:migrate && yarn db:seed` first.
- **Run it:** `DATABASE_URL=postgres://carma:carma@localhost:5432/carma yarn workspace @carma/api test` (or scope to the file with `... vitest run src/search/search.integration.test.ts`).

## If you want it less manual
Options, in order of how much I'd recommend them:

1. **Add a convenience script** (my recommendation) — e.g. a root `test:integration` that sets the URL and runs, so it's one command. Keeps `yarn test` DB-free.
2. **Leave as-is** and use the env prefix when you want the DB tests.
3. **Auto-load `.env` in a vitest config** — makes integration run automatically, but it also means `yarn test` would **fail** (connection refused) instead of skip whenever no DB is up, which loses the CI-safe property. I'd avoid this.

Want me to add the `test:integration` convenience script (option 1)?

{
  "file_path": "/Users/garythrels/Development/personal/carma/apps/api/src/features/articles/articles.filters.ts",
  "content": "import { and, eq, gte, lte, sql, type SQL } from \"drizzle-orm\";\nimport { parseQuery } from \"@carma/shared\";\nimport { articles } from \"../../db/schema.js\";\nimport { compileToTsquery } from \"../../search/compile.js\";\nimport type { ArticleFilterInput } from \"./articles.types.js\";\n\n/** Raised on malformed filter inputs; the router maps it to a 400. */\nexport class FilterError extends Error {\n  constructor(message: string) {\n    super(message);\n    this.name = \"FilterError\";\n  }\n}\n\n/** Parse a query param as a positive integer id, or throw FilterError. */\nfunction parseId(raw: unknown, field: string): number | undefined {\n  if (typeof raw !== \"string\" || raw.length === 0) return undefined;\n  const n = Number(raw);\n  if (!Number.isInteger(n) || n <= 0) {\n    throw new FilterError(`Invalid ${field}: expected a positive integer`);\n  }\n  return n;\n}\n\n/** Parse a query param as a date, or throw FilterError. */\nfunction parseDate(raw: unknown, field: string): Date | undefined {\n  if (typeof raw !== \"string\" || raw.length === 0) return undefined;\n  const d = new Date(raw);\n  if (Number.isNaN(d.getTime())) {\n    throw new FilterError(`Invalid ${field}: expected an ISO date`);\n  }\n  return d;\n}\n\n/**\n * Parse & validate the raw request query into a filter input. Either date bound\n * may be omitted, but if both are present `to` must not precede `from`.\n * Throws FilterError on malformed input.\n */\nexport function parseArticleFilters(query: Record<string, unknown>): ArticleFilterInput {\n  const from = parseDate(query.from, \"from\");\n  const to = parseDate(query.to, \"to\");\n  if (from && to && to.getTime() < from.getTime()) {\n    throw new FilterError(\"Invalid date range: 'to' must be on or after 'from'\");\n  }\n  return {\n    q: typeof query.q === \"string\" ? query.q : undefined,\n    sourceId: parseId(query.source, \"source\"),\n    languageId: parseId(query.language, \"language\"),\n    from,\n    to,\n  };\n}\n\n/** Full-text search predicate from a raw query string; may throw `ParseError`. */\nfunction searchFilter(q: string | undefined): SQL | undefined {\n  if (!q || q.trim().length === 0) return undefined;\n  const node = parseQuery(q);\n  return node ? sql`${articles.searchVector} @@ ${compileToTsquery(node)}` : undefined;\n}\n\n/**\n * Combine all active filters into a single predicate (or `undefined` when none\n * apply). All predicates are on `articles` columns, so they also apply cleanly\n * to the keyset existence probes. Throws `ParseError` for a malformed `q`.\n */\nexport function buildArticleFilters(input: ArticleFilterInput): SQL | undefined {\n  return and(\n    searchFilter(input.q),\n    input.sourceId !== undefined ? eq(articles.sourceId, input.sourceId) : undefined,\n    input.languageId !== undefined ? eq(articles.languageId, input.languageId) : undefined,\n    input.from ? gte(articles.publishedAt, input.from) : undefined,\n    input.to ? lte(articles.publishedAt, input.to) : undefined,\n  );\n}\n"
}

  "content": "import { afterAll, beforeAll, describe, expect, it } from \"vitest\";\nimport { drizzle, type NodePgDatabase } from \"drizzle-orm/node-postgres\";\nimport { Pool } from \"pg\";\nimport { asc, sql } from \"drizzle-orm\";\nimport { articles } from \"../../db/schema.js\";\nimport { buildArticleFilters } from \"./articles.filters.js\";\nimport type { ArticleFilterInput } from \"./articles.types.js\";\n\n/*\n * Runs against a migrated + seeded Postgres. Skipped when DATABASE_URL is unset.\n *   DATABASE_URL=postgres://carma:carma@localhost:5432/carma yarn workspace @carma/api test\n *\n * Seed facts used below: every sample article has a unique source, so source id\n * N ↔ article N. Languages seed in first-appearance order: en=1, ar=2, zh=3\n * (article 8 is Arabic, article 9 is Chinese).\n */\nconst url = process.env.DATABASE_URL;\n\ndescribe.skipIf(!url)(\"article filters (integration)\", () => {\n  let pool: Pool;\n  let db: NodePgDatabase;\n\n  beforeAll(async () => {\n    pool = new Pool({ connectionString: url });\n    db = drizzle(pool);\n    const counts = await db.select({ count: sql<number>`count(*)::int` }).from(articles);\n    if ((counts[0]?.count ?? 0) < 20) {\n      throw new Error(\"Expected the seeded dataset (>=20 articles).\");\n    }\n  });\n\n  afterAll(async () => {\n    await pool.end();\n  });\n\n  /** Apply a filter input and return matching article ids (ascending). */\n  async function filter(input: ArticleFilterInput): Promise<number[]> {\n    const rows = await db\n      .select({ id: articles.id })\n      .from(articles)\n      .where(buildArticleFilters(input))\n      .orderBy(asc(articles.id));\n    return rows.map((r) => r.id);\n  }\n\n  it(\"filters by source id\", async () => {\n    expect(await filter({ sourceId: 1 })).toEqual([1]);\n  });\n\n  it(\"filters by language id\", async () => {\n    expect(await filter({ languageId: 2 })).toEqual([8]); // Arabic\n    expect(await filter({ languageId: 3 })).toEqual([9]); // Chinese\n  });\n\n  it(\"filters by a lower date bound (from)\", async () => {\n    const ids = await filter({ from: new Date(\"2026-07-10T00:00:00.000Z\") });\n    expect(ids).toEqual(expect.arrayContaining([1, 2, 3]));\n    expect(ids).not.toContain(20); // published 2026-06-12\n  });\n\n  it(\"filters by a from..to window\", async () => {\n    const ids = await filter({\n      from: new Date(\"2026-07-08T00:00:00.000Z\"),\n      to: new Date(\"2026-07-10T23:59:59.999Z\"),\n    });\n    expect(ids).toEqual([3, 4, 5]); // 07-10, 07-09, 07-08\n  });\n\n  it(\"combines search with a source filter (AND)\", async () => {\n    expect(await filter({ sourceId: 5, q: \"renew*\" })).toEqual([5]); // The Guardian + renewable\n    expect(await filter({ sourceId: 1, q: \"renew*\" })).toEqual([]); // Reuters isn't renewable\n  });\n});\n"
}

  "content": "import { ApiResponse, Lookups } from \"@carma/shared\";\nimport { useEffect, useState } from \"react\";\n\nconst EMPTY: Lookups = { sources: [], languages: [] };\n\n/** Fetch the filter reference data (sources + languages) once on mount. */\nexport function useLookups(): Lookups {\n  const [lookups, setLookups] = useState<Lookups>(EMPTY);\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    const controller = new AbortController();\n    fetch(\"/api/lookups\", { signal: controller.signal })\n      .then((res) => (res.ok ? res.json() : Promise.reject(new Error(String(res.status)))))\n      .then((body: ApiResponse<Lookups>) => setLookups(body.data))\n      .catch(() => {\n        // Non-fatal: filters just render with no options if this fails.\n      });\n    return () => controller.abort();\n  }, []);\n\n  return lookups;\n}\n"
}

  "content": "import { useState } from \"react\";\nimport { Language, Source } from \"@carma/shared\";\n\n/** The filter values this control emits (dates are `yyyy-mm-dd` or null). */\nexport interface FilterValue {\n  sourceId: number | null;\n  languageId: number | null;\n  from: string | null;\n  to: string | null;\n}\n\ninterface Props {\n  sources: Source[];\n  languages: Language[];\n  onChange: (value: FilterValue) => void;\n}\n\n/**\n * Source + language dropdowns and an independent from/to date range. Either date\n * may be left empty; if both are set, `to` must be on or after `from` — an\n * invalid range shows an error and is not applied (other changes still apply).\n */\nexport function Filters({ sources, languages, onChange }: Props) {\n  const [sourceId, setSourceId] = useState<number | null>(null);\n  const [languageId, setLanguageId] = useState<number | null>(null);\n  const [from, setFrom] = useState(\"\");\n  const [to, setTo] = useState(\"\");\n\n  const rangeInvalid = from !== \"\" && to !== \"\" && to < from;\n\n  // Apply the current selection unless the date range is invalid.\n  function apply(next: {\n    sourceId: number | null;\n    languageId: number | null;\n    from: string;\n    to: string;\n  }) {\n    if (next.from !== \"\" && next.to !== \"\" && next.to < next.from) return;\n    onChange({\n      sourceId: next.sourceId,\n      languageId: next.languageId,\n      from: next.from || null,\n      to: next.to || null,\n    });\n  }\n\n  function onSource(value: string) {\n    const id = value === \"\" ? null : Number(value);\n    setSourceId(id);\n    apply({ sourceId: id, languageId, from, to });\n  }\n  function onLanguage(value: string) {\n    const id = value === \"\" ? null : Number(value);\n    setLanguageId(id);\n    apply({ sourceId, languageId: id, from, to });\n  }\n  function onFrom(value: string) {\n    setFrom(value);\n    apply({ sourceId, languageId, from: value, to });\n  }\n  function onTo(value: string) {\n    setTo(value);\n    apply({ sourceId, languageId, from, to: value });\n  }\n  function clear() {\n    setSourceId(null);\n    setLanguageId(null);\n    setFrom(\"\");\n    setTo(\"\");\n    onChange({ sourceId: null, languageId: null, from: null, to: null });\n  }\n\n  const active =\n    sourceId !== null || languageId !== null || from !== \"\" || to !== \"\";\n\n  return (\n    <div className=\"filters\">\n      <div className=\"filters-row\">\n        <label className=\"field\">\n          <span>Source</span>\n          <select value={sourceId ?? \"\"} onChange={(e) => onSource(e.target.value)}>\n            <option value=\"\">All sources</option>\n            {sources.map((s) => (\n              <option key={s.id} value={s.id}>\n                {s.name}\n              </option>\n            ))}\n          </select>\n        </label>\n\n        <label className=\"field\">\n          <span>Language</span>\n          <select value={languageId ?? \"\"} onChange={(e) => onLanguage(e.target.value)}>\n            <option value=\"\">All languages</option>\n            {languages.map((l) => (\n              <option key={l.id} value={l.id}>\n                {l.name}\n              </option>\n            ))}\n          </select>\n        </label>\n\n        <label className=\"field\">\n          <span>From</span>\n          <input\n            type=\"date\"\n            value={from}\n            max={to || undefined}\n            onChange={(e) => onFrom(e.target.value)}\n            aria-invalid={rangeInvalid}\n          />\n        </label>\n\n        <label className=\"field\">\n          <span>To</span>\n          <input\n            type=\"date\"\n            value={to}\n            min={from || undefined}\n            onChange={(e) => onTo(e.target.value)}\n            aria-invalid={rangeInvalid}\n          />\n        </label>\n\n        <button type=\"button\" className=\"filters-clear\" onClick={clear} disabled={!active}>\n          Clear filters\n        </button>\n      </div>\n      {rangeInvalid && (\n        <p className=\"filters-error\">‘To’ date must be on or after ‘From’ date.</p>\n      )}\n    </div>\n  );\n}\n"
}

  "content": "import { Paginated, Article, ApiError } from \"@carma/shared\";\nimport { useEffect, useRef, useState } from \"react\";\nimport { ArticleQuery, ArticlesState } from \"../types\";\nimport { useCursorPagination } from \"./useCursorPagination\";\n\n/** Build the API query params from a request cursor + the article query. */\nfunction buildParams(\n  request: { cursor: string | null; direction: \"next\" | \"prev\" },\n  query: ArticleQuery,\n  limit: number,\n): string {\n  const params = new URLSearchParams({ limit: String(limit) });\n  if (request.cursor) {\n    params.set(\"cursor\", request.cursor);\n    params.set(\"direction\", request.direction);\n  }\n  const q = query.q.trim();\n  if (q) params.set(\"q\", q);\n  if (query.sourceId !== null) params.set(\"source\", String(query.sourceId));\n  if (query.languageId !== null) params.set(\"language\", String(query.languageId));\n  // Date inputs are `yyyy-mm-dd`; widen to full-day UTC bounds so the range is\n  // inclusive of both endpoints.\n  if (query.from) params.set(\"from\", `${query.from}T00:00:00.000Z`);\n  if (query.to) params.set(\"to\", `${query.to}T23:59:59.999Z`);\n  return params.toString();\n}\n\n/**\n * Keyset-paginated articles for a given search + filter query. Any change to the\n * query snaps pagination back to page one (via useCursorPagination's reset key).\n */\nexport function useArticles(query: ArticleQuery, limit = 5) {\n  const [state, setState] = useState<ArticlesState>({ status: \"loading\" });\n  const [isFetching, setIsFetching] = useState(true);\n  // Skip the scroll-to-top on the very first load (already at the top).\n  const isInitialLoad = useRef(true);\n\n  const pageInfo = state.status === \"ready\" ? state.pageInfo : null;\n  // A primitive key that changes whenever any part of the query changes.\n  const resetKey = JSON.stringify(query);\n  const { request, goNext, goPrev } = useCursorPagination(pageInfo, resetKey);\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    const controller = new AbortController();\n    setIsFetching(true);\n\n    async function load() {\n      try {\n        const res = await fetch(`/api/articles?${buildParams(request, query, limit)}`, {\n          signal: controller.signal,\n        });\n        if (!res.ok) {\n          let message = `Request failed: ${res.status}`;\n          try {\n            const body = (await res.json()) as ApiError;\n            if (body?.error) message = body.error;\n          } catch {\n            /* keep the status-based message */\n          }\n          throw new Error(message);\n        }\n        const body = (await res.json()) as Paginated<Article>;\n        setState({\n          status: \"ready\",\n          articles: body.data,\n          pageInfo: body.pageInfo,\n        });\n        if (isInitialLoad.current) {\n          isInitialLoad.current = false;\n        } else {\n          window.scrollTo({ top: 0, behavior: \"smooth\" });\n        }\n      } catch (err) {\n        if (controller.signal.aborted) return;\n        setState({\n          status: \"error\",\n          message: err instanceof Error ? err.message : \"Unknown error\",\n        });\n      } finally {\n        if (!controller.signal.aborted) setIsFetching(false);\n      }\n    }\n\n    void load();\n    return () => controller.abort();\n    // `resetKey` captures every field of `query`; `request` covers pagination.\n    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps\n  }, [request, limit, resetKey]);\n\n  return { state, isFetching, goNext, goPrev };\n}\n"
}

  "content": "import { useState } from \"react\";\nimport { ArticleListItem } from \"./components/ArticleListItem\";\nimport { EmptyState } from \"./components/EmptyState\";\nimport { SearchBar } from \"./components/SearchBar\";\nimport { Filters, type FilterValue } from \"./components/Filters\";\nimport { useArticles } from \"./hooks/useArticles\";\nimport { useLookups } from \"./hooks/useLookups\";\nimport { ArticleQuery, EMPTY_QUERY } from \"./types\";\n\nexport function App() {\n  const [query, setQuery] = useState<ArticleQuery>(EMPTY_QUERY);\n  const lookups = useLookups();\n  const { state, isFetching, goNext, goPrev } = useArticles(query);\n\n  const setSearch = (q: string) => setQuery((prev) => ({ ...prev, q }));\n  const setFilters = (f: FilterValue) => setQuery((prev) => ({ ...prev, ...f }));\n\n  const hasQuery =\n    query.q.trim().length > 0 ||\n    query.sourceId !== null ||\n    query.languageId !== null ||\n    query.from !== null ||\n    query.to !== null;\n\n  const canPrev =\n    state.status === \"ready\" && state.pageInfo.hasPrev && !isFetching;\n  const canNext =\n    state.status === \"ready\" && state.pageInfo.hasNext && !isFetching;\n\n  return (\n    <main className=\"container\">\n      <h1>Carma</h1>\n      <h4>by Gary Hili</h4>\n      <p className=\"subtitle\">\n        Articles served from Postgres via Express + Drizzle.\n      </p>\n\n      <SearchBar onSearch={setSearch} />\n      <Filters\n        sources={lookups.sources}\n        languages={lookups.languages}\n        onChange={setFilters}\n      />\n\n      {state.status === \"error\" ? (\n        <p className=\"error\">Failed to load articles: {state.message}</p>\n      ) : state.status !== \"ready\" || state.articles.length === 0 ? (\n        <EmptyState loading={state.status !== \"ready\"} hasQuery={hasQuery} />\n      ) : (\n        <>\n          <ul className=\"articles\" aria-busy={isFetching}>\n            {state.articles.map((article) => (\n              <ArticleListItem key={article.id} article={article} />\n            ))}\n          </ul>\n          <nav className=\"pager\" aria-label=\"Pagination\">\n            <button type=\"button\" onClick={goPrev} disabled={!canPrev}>\n              ← Newer\n            </button>\n            <span className=\"pager-status\">\n              {isFetching ? \"Loading…\" : `${state.articles.length} shown`}\n            </span>\n            <button type=\"button\" onClick={goNext} disabled={!canNext}>\n              Older →\n            </button>\n          </nav>\n        </>\n      )}\n    </main>\n  );\n}\n"
}

1	import { and, eq, gte, lte, sql, type SQL } from "drizzle-orm";
2	import { parseQuery } from "@carma/shared";
3	import { articles } from "../../db/schema.js";
4	import { compileToTsquery } from "../../search/compile.js";
5	import type { ArticleFilterInput } from "./articles.types.js";
6	
7	/** Raised on malformed filter inputs; the router maps it to a 400. */
8	export class FilterError extends Error {
9	  constructor(message: string) {
10	    super(message);
11	    this.name = "FilterError";
12	  }
13	}
14	
15	/** Parse a query param as a positive integer id, or throw FilterError. */
16	function parseId(raw: unknown, field: string): number | undefined {
17	  if (typeof raw !== "string" || raw.length === 0) return undefined;
18	  const n = Number(raw);
19	  if (!Number.isInteger(n) || n <= 0) {
20	    throw new FilterError(`Invalid ${field}: expected a positive integer`);
21	  }
22	  return n;
23	}
24	
25	/** Parse a query param as a date, or throw FilterError. */
26	function parseDate(raw: unknown, field: string): Date | undefined {
27	  if (typeof raw !== "string" || raw.length === 0) return undefined;
28	  const d = new Date(raw);
29	  if (Number.isNaN(d.getTime())) {
30	    throw new FilterError(`Invalid ${field}: expected an ISO date`);
31	  }
32	  return d;
33	}
34	
35	/**
36	 * Parse & validate the raw request query into a filter input. Either date bound
37	 * may be omitted, but if both are present `to` must not precede `from`.
38	 * Throws FilterError on malformed input.
39	 */
40	export function parseArticleFilters(
41	  query: Record<string, unknown>,
42	): ArticleFilterInput {
43	  const from = parseDate(query.from, "from");
44	  const to = parseDate(query.to, "to");
45	  if (from && to && to.getTime() < from.getTime()) {
46	    throw new FilterError(
47	      "Invalid date range: 'to' must be on or after 'from'",
48	    );
49	  }
50	  return {
51	    q: typeof query.q === "string" ? query.q : undefined,
52	    sourceId: parseId(query.source, "source"),
53	    languageId: parseId(query.language, "language"),
54	    from,
55	    to,
56	  };
57	}
58	
59	/** Full-text search predicate from a raw query string; may throw `ParseError`. */
60	function searchFilter(q: string | undefined): SQL | undefined {
61	  if (!q || q.trim().length === 0) return undefined;
62	  const node = parseQuery(q);
63	  return node
64	    ? sql`${articles.searchVector} @@ ${compileToTsquery(node)}`
65	    : undefined;
66	}
67	
68	/**
69	 * Combine all active filters into a single predicate (or `undefined` when none
70	 * apply). All predicates are on `articles` columns, so they also apply cleanly
71	 * to the keyset existence probes. Throws `ParseError` for a malformed `q`.
72	 */
73	export function buildArticleFilters(
74	  input: ArticleFilterInput,
75	): SQL | undefined {
76	  return and(
77	    searchFilter(input.q),
78	    input.sourceId !== undefined
79	      ? eq(articles.sourceId, input.sourceId)
80	      : undefined,
81	    input.languageId !== undefined
82	      ? eq(articles.languageId, input.languageId)
83	      : undefined,
84	    input.from ? gte(articles.publishedAt, input.from) : undefined,
85	    input.to ? lte(articles.publishedAt, input.to) : undefined,
86	  );
87	}
88
