{
  "file_path": "/Users/garythrels/Development/personal/carma/apps/web/src/hooks/useAggregate.ts",
  "content": "import { ApiResponse, SentimentBucket, TimeInterval } from \"@carma/shared\";\nimport { useEffect, useState } from \"react\";\n\nexport interface AggregateParams {\n  interval: TimeInterval;\n  sourceId: number | null;\n}\n\ninterface State {\n  buckets: SentimentBucket[];\n  loading: boolean;\n  error: string | null;\n}\n\n/** Fetch per-(bucket, sentiment) article counts for the interval + source. */\nexport function useAggregate(params: AggregateParams): State {\n  const [state, setState] = useState<State>({\n    buckets: [],\n    loading: true,\n    error: null,\n  });\n\n  const key = JSON.stringify(params);\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    const controller = new AbortController();\n    setState((s) => ({ ...s, loading: true, error: null }));\n\n    const qs = new URLSearchParams({ interval: params.interval });\n    if (params.sourceId !== null) qs.set(\"source\", String(params.sourceId));\n\n    fetch(`/api/articles/aggregate?${qs.toString()}`, { signal: controller.signal })\n      .then((res) =>\n        res.ok ? res.json() : Promise.reject(new Error(`Request failed: ${res.status}`)),\n      )\n      .then((body: ApiResponse<SentimentBucket[]>) =>\n        setState({ buckets: body.data, loading: false, error: null }),\n      )\n      .catch((err: unknown) => {\n        if (controller.signal.aborted) return;\n        setState({\n          buckets: [],\n          loading: false,\n          error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : \"Unknown error\",\n        });\n      });\n\n    return () => controller.abort();\n    // `key` captures every param field.\n    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps\n  }, [key]);\n\n  return state;\n}\n"
}

0),\n      borderColor: SERIES[s].color,\n      backgroundColor: SERIES[s].color,\n      borderDash: SERIES[s].dash,\n      pointStyle: SERIES[s].point,\n      borderWidth: 2,\n      pointRadius: 4,\n      pointHoverRadius: 6,\n      tension: 0.3,\n      fill: false,\n    })),\n  };\n\n  const options: ChartOptions<\"line\"> = {\n    responsive: true,\n    maintainAspectRatio: false,\n    interaction: { mode: \"index\", intersect: false },\n    plugins: {\n      legend: {\n        position: \"bottom\",\n        labels: { usePointStyle: true, color: TICK, boxWidth: 8 },\n      },\n      tooltip: { mode: \"index\", intersect: false },\n    },\n    scales: {\n      x: { grid: { color: GRID }, ticks: { color: TICK } },\n      y: {\n        beginAtZero: true,\n        grid: { color: GRID },\n        ticks: { color: TICK, precision: 0 },\n      },\n    },\n  };\n\n  return (\n    <section className=\"chart-card\">\n      <div className=\"chart-header\">\n        <h3>Articles over time by sentiment</h3>\n        <div className=\"chart-controls\">\n          <div className=\"interval-toggle\" role=\"group\" aria-label=\"Interval\">\n            {INTERVALS.map((iv) => (\n              <button\n                key={iv}\n                type=\"button\"\n                className={interval === iv ? \"active\" : \"\"}\n                aria-pressed={interval === iv}\n                onClick={() => setInterval(iv)}\n              >\n                {iv === \"month\" ? \"Month\" : \"Week\"}\n              </button>\n            ))}\n          </div>\n\n          <label className=\"field\">\n            <span>Source</span>\n            <select\n              value={sourceId ?? \"\"}\n              onChange={(e) =>\n                setSourceId(e.target.value ? Number(e.target.value) : null)\n              }\n            >\n              <option value=\"\">All sources</option>\n              {sources.map((s) => (\n                <option key={s.id} value={s.id}>\n                  {s.name}\n                </option>\n              ))}\n            </select>\n          </label>\n        </div>\n      </div>\n\n      <div className=\"chart-canvas\" aria-busy={loading}>\n        {error ? (\n          <p className=\"error\">Failed to load chart: {error}</p>\n        ) : labels.length === 0 && !loading ? (\n          <p className=\"chart-empty\">No classified articles for this selection.</p>\n        ) : (\n          <Line\n            data={data}\n            options={options}\n            aria-label=\"Article counts over time by sentiment\"\n          />\n        )}\n      </div>\n    </section>\n  );\n}\n"

## What changed
**Backend** — `/aggregate` now groups by `(bucket, sentiment)`:
- `getSentimentBuckets({ interval, sourceId })` — `date_trunc(interval, published_at)` × `sentiment`, `count(*)`, inner-joined to enrichment with `sentiment IS NOT NULL`, source-only filter. Shared `AggregateBucket` → **`SentimentBucket { bucket, sentiment, count }`**. Sentiment param dropped from parsing.

**Frontend** — multi-line chart:
- One `<Line>` dataset per sentiment (data pivoted from the flat rows onto sorted buckets, missing→0). Source select + Month/Week toggle only; sentiment select removed.
- **Accessibility (the interesting part):** I ran the dataviz validator, which caught that `positive`(green)↔`negative`(red) collapse under red-green CVD (ΔE ≈ 4, below the floor). Rather than abandon the intuitive badge colours, I made **colour non-load-bearing** — each line has a distinct **marker shape + dash pattern** and a **labelled legend**, so it's fully readable in grayscale. Documented in the component + README, with small-multiples noted as the stricter alternative.

## Verified
- Full suite green **×3** (24 shared + 44 API, no flakiness).
- **Fixed a test race** I introduced: the enrichment integration test mutates articles 1–2 while the aggregate test asserted on them — added `apps/api/vitest.config.ts` with `fileParallelism: false` so the shared-DB integration files run serially.
- Live: month → 7 rows / 2 buckets, per-sentiment `{positive:10, negative:4, neutral:4, mixed:2}` = 20; week 13 rows; `source=1` → 1; `interval=bogus` → 400; correct shape through the Vite proxy; web 200.
- README + typecheck + web build all updated/clean.

## One heads-up
Running the enrichment **integration tests against your live docker DB overwrote articles 1 & 2's enrichment with mock (`neutral`)** output — they'd held real LLM sentiments before. To restore the real values: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=… yarn db:enrich 1 --force` and `… 2 --force`. (This is inherent to pointing the mutating integration tests at the dev volume; the aggregate still renders fine either way.)

`docker compose down` when done (volume kept).

{
  "file_path": "/Users/garythrels/Development/personal/carma/apps/api/src/features/articles/articles.aggregate.ts",
  "content": "import { eq, sql } from \"drizzle-orm\";\nimport type { AggregateBucket, Sentiment, TimeInterval } from \"@carma/shared\";\nimport { db } from \"../../db/index.js\";\nimport { articleEnrichments, articles } from \"../../db/schema.js\";\nimport { FilterError, parseId } from \"./articles.filters.js\";\n\n// Whitelist of allowed date_trunc granularities. Only these literals are ever\n// interpolated into SQL — never raw request input — so the interval can't be an\n// injection vector.\nconst INTERVALS: Record<string, TimeInterval> = { month: \"month\", week: \"week\" };\n\nconst SENTIMENTS: Sentiment[] = [\"positive\", \"negative\", \"neutral\", \"mixed\"];\n\nexport interface AggregateParams {\n  interval: TimeInterval;\n  sourceId?: number;\n}\n\n/** Parse & validate aggregate query params. Throws FilterError on bad input. */\nexport function parseAggregateParams(\n  query: Record<string, unknown>,\n): AggregateParams {\n  const rawInterval = typeof query.interval === \"string\" ? query.interval : \"month\";\n  const interval = INTERVALS[rawInterval];\n  if (!interval) {\n    throw new FilterError(\"Invalid interval: expected 'month' or 'week'\");\n  }\n  return { interval, sourceId: parseId(query.source, \"source\") };\n}\n\n/**\n * Per-time-bucket article counts: an overall `total` (LEFT JOIN → counts every\n * article, classified or not) plus a per-sentiment breakdown via conditional\n * aggregation. One grouped query, ascending by bucket. Optionally restricted to\n * one source. `interval` is a whitelisted literal (see INTERVALS).\n */\nexport async function getAggregateBuckets({\n  interval,\n  sourceId,\n}: AggregateParams): Promise<AggregateBucket[]> {\n  const bucket = sql<string>`date_trunc(${sql.raw(`'${interval}'`)}, ${articles.publishedAt})`;\n  // count(*) FILTER (WHERE sentiment = $s) — sentiment values are a fixed enum,\n  // bound as params and compared as text (avoids enum-vs-text operator issues).\n  const per = (s: Sentiment) =>\n    sql<number>`(count(*) filter (where ${articleEnrichments.sentiment}::text = ${s}))::int`;\n\n  const query = db\n    .select({\n      bucket,\n      total: sql<number>`count(*)::int`,\n      positive: per(\"positive\"),\n      negative: per(\"negative\"),\n      neutral: per(\"neutral\"),\n      mixed: per(\"mixed\"),\n    })\n    .from(articles)\n    .leftJoin(articleEnrichments, eq(articleEnrichments.articleId, articles.id))\n    .$dynamic();\n\n  if (sourceId !== undefined) query.where(eq(articles.sourceId, sourceId));\n\n  const rows = await query.groupBy(bucket).orderBy(bucket);\n\n  return rows.map((r) => ({\n    bucket: new Date(r.bucket).toISOString(),\n    total: r.total,\n    bySentiment: {\n      positive: r.positive,\n      negative: r.negative,\n      neutral: r.neutral,\n      mixed: r.mixed,\n    },\n  }));\n}\n\nexport { SENTIMENTS };\n"
}

beforeAll(async () => {\n    ({ getAggregateBuckets } = await import(\"./articles.aggregate.js\"));\n    schema = await import(\"../../db/schema.js\");\n    pool = new Pool({ connectionString: url });\n    db = drizzle(pool);\n    const c = await db\n      .select({ n: sql<number>`count(*)::int` })\n      .from(schema.articles);\n    if ((c[0]?.n ?? 0) < 20) {\n      throw new Error(\"Expected 0);\n\n  it(\"bucket totals sum to the full article count (all articles)\", async () => {\n    const total =\n      (await db.select({ n: sql<number>`count(*)::int` }).from(schema.articles))[0]!\n expect(week.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(month.length);\n    expect(sumTotal(week)).toBe(sumTotal(month));\n  });\n\n  it(\"filters by source\", async () => {\n    // Each sample article has a Done — a bold **Total** line now sits above the four sentiment lines, live at **http://localhost:5173**.

## What changed
- **Backend** — one grouped query now computes both in a single pass:
  - `total` via **`LEFT JOIN`** + `count(*)` → counts **every** article in the bucket, even unclassified ones (so it's a true total, not just the sum of the sentiment lines).
  - the per-sentiment breakdown via `count(*) FILTER (WHERE sentiment = …)`.
  - Response type: `SentimentBucket[]` → **`AggregateBucket { bucket, total, bySentiment }`**.
- **Frontend** — a 5th dataset "Total" with a **distinct blue hue, thicker line (3px), and star markers** so it reads as the aggregate, drawn above the four sentiment lines; the per-sentiment lines keep their shape+dash+legend encoding. Buckets now arrive pre-shaped (total + all four counts), so the frontend no longer pivots.

## Verified
- Typecheck + web build clean; **45 tests** green (aggregate unit 4, integration 5) — including new invariants: **bucket totals sum to the full article count** and **`total ≥ sum(bySentiment)` in every bucket**.
- Live: `Jun total=8`, `Jul total=12`, `bySentiment` sums match, `source=1` → total 1, web 200. README + API-surface row updated.

Design note: "total" counts all articles regardless of sentiment (`LEFT JOIN`), while the sentiment lines only count classified ones — so if some articles were ever unenriched, the Total line would sit above the summed sentiments, which is the intended read. Right now everything's classified, so they coincide.

`docker compose down` when you're done. Anything else on the chart, or is this a good stopping point?

One thing I already noticed while scoping (the verifier will confirm or drop it): `EnrichmentView.tsx` was just edited to nest a `<div className="enrichment-label">` **inside a `<p>`** — invalid HTML (a `<div>` can't be a child of `<p>`; the browser auto-closes the `<p>`, and React will warn about DOM nesting). Not a security issue, but a real bug worth fixing. I'll fold it into the results.

I'll wait for the workflow's verified findings before making any changes.

1	import { eq, sql } from "drizzle-orm";
2	import type { AggregateBucket, Sentiment, TimeInterval } from "@carma/shared";
3	import { db } from "../../db/index.js";
4	import { articleEnrichments, articles } from "../../db/schema.js";
5	import { FilterError, parseId } from "./articles.filters.js";
6	
7	// Whitelist of allowed date_trunc granularities. Only these literals are ever
8	// interpolated into SQL — never raw request input — so the interval can't be an
9	// injection vector.
10	const INTERVALS: Record<string, TimeInterval> = { month: "month", week: "week" };
11	
12	export interface AggregateParams {
13	  interval: TimeInterval;
14	  sourceId?: number;
15	}
16	
17	/** Parse & validate aggregate query params. Throws FilterError on bad input. */
18	export function parseAggregateParams(
19	  query: Record<string, unknown>,
20	): AggregateParams {
21	  const rawInterval = typeof query.interval === "string" ? query.interval : "month";
22	  const interval = INTERVALS[rawInterval];
23	  if (!interval) {
24	    throw new FilterError("Invalid interval: expected 'month' or 'week'");
25	  }
26	  return { interval, sourceId: parseId(query.source, "source") };
27	}
28	
29	/**
30	 * Per-time-bucket article counts: an overall `total` (LEFT JOIN → counts every
31	 * article, classified or not) plus a per-sentiment breakdown via conditional
32	 * aggregation. One grouped query, ascending by bucket. Optionally restricted to
33	 * one source. `interval` is a whitelisted literal (see INTERVALS).
34	 */
35	export async function getAggregateBuckets({
36	  interval,
37	  sourceId,
38	}: AggregateParams): Promise<AggregateBucket[]> {
39	  const bucket = sql<string>`date_trunc(${sql.raw(`'${interval}'`)}, ${articles.publishedAt})`;
40	  // count(*) FILTER (WHERE sentiment = $s) — sentiment values are a fixed enum,
41	  // bound as params and compared as text (avoids enum-vs-text operator issues).
42	  const per = (s: Sentiment) =>
43	    sql<number>`(count(*) filter (where ${articleEnrichments.sentiment}::text = ${s}))::int`;
44	
45	  const query = db
46	    .select({
47	      bucket,
48	      total: sql<number>`count(*)::int`,
49	      positive: per("positive"),
50	      negative: per("negative"),
51	      neutral: per("neutral"),
52	      mixed: per("mixed"),
53	    })
54	    .from(articles)
55	    .leftJoin(articleEnrichments, eq(articleEnrichments.articleId, articles.id))
56	    .$dynamic();
57	
58	  if (sourceId !== undefined) query.where(eq(articles.sourceId, sourceId));
59	
60	  const rows = await query.groupBy(bucket).orderBy(bucket);
61	
62	  return rows.map((r) => ({
63	    bucket: new Date(r.bucket).toISOString(),
64	    total: r.total,
65	    bySentiment: {
66	      positive: r.positive,
67	      negative: r.negative,
68	      neutral: r.neutral,
69	      mixed: r.mixed,
70	    },
71	  }));
72	}
73	
```

50	      ? req.query.cursor

1	import { sql, type SQL } from "drizzle-orm";
2	import type { PageInfo } from "@carma/shared";
3	import { articles } from "../../db/schema.js";
4	import { decodeCursor, encodeCursor } from "../../lib/cursor.js";
5	import type { Direction, KeysetAnchor } from "./articles.types.js";
6	
7	/**
8	 * Keyset (cursor) pagination for the article feed, ordered `(published_at DESC,
9	 * id DESC)`. Everything specific to *how we page* lives here: request parsing,
10	 * index-matching ordering, keyset predicates, and cursor-token ↔ position
11	 * translation. The repository runs queries with these; the router speaks HTTP.
12	 */
13	
14	export const DEFAULT_LIMIT = 5;
15	export const MAX_LIMIT = 50;
16	
17	export const EMPTY_PAGE_INFO: PageInfo = {
18	  cursor: null,
19	  hasNext: false,
20	  hasPrev: false,
21	};
22	
23	export function parseLimit(raw: unknown): number {
24	  const n = Number(raw);
25	  if (Number.isInteger(n) && n > 0) return Math.min(n, MAX_LIMIT);
26	  return DEFAULT_LIMIT;
27	}
28	
29	export function parseDirection(raw: unknown): Direction {
30	  return raw === "prev" ? "prev" : "next";
31	}
32	
33	// Ordering matches the articles_published_at_id_idx index. NULLS LAST/FIRST is
34	// required so the planner uses the index instead of sorting (see README).
35	const ORDER_DESC = sql`${articles.publishedAt} DESC NULLS LAST, ${articles.id} DESC NULLS LAST`;
36	const ORDER_ASC = sql`${articles.publishedAt} ASC NULLS FIRST, ${articles.id} ASC NULLS FIRST`;
37	
38	/** Feed order for a direction; backward pages scan ascending, then get reversed. */
39	export function orderFor(direction: Direction): SQL {
40	  return direction === "prev" ? ORDER_ASC : ORDER_DESC;
41	}
42	
43	/** Rows strictly older than the anchor. */
44	export function olderThan(a: KeysetAnchor): SQL {
45	  return sql`(${articles.publishedAt}, ${articles.id}) < (${a.publishedAt}, ${a.id})`;
46	}
47	
48	/** Rows strictly newer than the anchor. */
49	export function newerThan(a: KeysetAnchor): SQL {
50	  return sql`(${articles.publishedAt}, ${articles.id}) > (${a.publishedAt}, ${a.id})`;
51	}
52	
53	/** Keyset predicate to page from an anchor: older for `next`, newer for `prev`. */
54	export function keysetPredicate(a: KeysetAnchor, direction: Direction): SQL {
55	  return direction === "prev" ? newerThan(a) : olderThan(a);
56	}
57	
58	/** Decode a cursor token to the anchor for this direction (throws CursorError). */
59	export function anchorFromCursor(
60	  token: string,
61	  direction: Direction,
62	): KeysetAnchor {
63	  const cursor = decodeCursor(token);
64	  const edge = direction === "prev" ? cursor.f : cursor.l;
65	  return { publishedAt: new Date(edge.t), id: edge.i };
66	}
67	
68	/** Build PageInfo (both-edges cursor token + flags) from a page's edges. */
69	export function buildPageInfo(
70	  first: KeysetAnchor,
71	  last: KeysetAnchor,
72	  hasNext: boolean,
73	  hasPrev: boolean,
74	): PageInfo {
75	  const cursor = encodeCursor({
76	    f: { t: first.publishedAt.toISOString(), i: first.id },
77	    l: { t: last.publishedAt.toISOString(), i: last.id },
78	  });
79	  return { cursor, hasNext, hasPrev };
80	}
81	
```

36	
37	I'll help you plan this out. Since you're new to Postgres and migration tools, let me give you a real comparison of Drizzle vs Prisma first — that's the one decision that meaningfully shapes the rest of the setup. Everything else (Yarn workspaces, Express, Vite/React, shared types, Docker Compose) is fairly standard and I'll lay it out after you pick.
38	
39	## Drizzle vs Prisma
40	
41	Both are excellent, TypeScript-first, and will handle your migrations. They represent two different philosophies.
42	
43	### Prisma
44	You define your schema in a dedicated `schema.prisma` file (its own declarative language). Prisma generates a typed client and generates migrations for you by diffing your schema against the DB.
45	
46	**Pros**
47	- **Most beginner-friendly.** Best-in-class docs, huge community, tons of tutorials.
48	- **Declarative schema** — you describe the shape you want, Prisma figures out the SQL migration (`prisma migrate dev`).
49	- **Prisma Studio** — a built-in GUI to browse/edit your database. Genuinely great when you're learning.
50	- Relations and nested queries are very ergonomic.
51	- Strong guardrails; hard to shoot yourself in the foot.
52	
53	**Cons**
54	- **Abstracts SQL away** — you learn "Prisma," not Postgres. As someone wanting to learn Postgres, you'll see less of what's actually happening.
55	- Heavier: a code-generation step (`prisma generate`) and historically a separate query engine binary (matters a little for Docker image size / cold starts).
56	- Its own schema DSL, not TypeScript.
57	- Raw/complex SQL queries are less natural; you drop out of the nice API.
58	
59	### Drizzle
60	You define your schema **in TypeScript**, and the query API is intentionally SQL-shaped (`db.select().from(users).where(...)`).
